findings.reason: it sends the §2 builder to the wrong call site, so a declared §1 feature (`--at`) lands inert for panes and the section's gate cannot pass as written.
findings.text: §2 says the sweep "is called from the same point of the producer poll as `_sweep_lift_rows` in `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py`", and `_sweep_lift_rows` is invoked inside the document-change gate `if sweep:` (recovery_watch.py:2702–2710); but §1 gives the record a `--at <ISO-8601>` option, so a reset's moment to fire is a clock instant, not a document write, and once the announcement's single document change has been folded the gate stays shut when `reset_at` passes — the row is never appended, and §2's own done-when ("a reset whose `reset_at` is still ahead appends no row until it passes") is unreachable for that input. The existing code puts its clock-driven sweeps outside that gate for exactly this reason (the comment immediately below the lift call, recovery_watch.py:2714–2720, says a gate waiting on a document would never fire).

findings.reason: the hook-context rule and the reach report are unrelated mechanisms reachable by different callers, and only a split lets each gate prove its own claim rather than one verdict covering both.
findings.text: §3's deliverable is three things under one node and one gate: the coordinator-obligations-hook line in `reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py`, the `reckon crew budget --announce-reset` reach report, and a paragraph committed to `~/Code/dotfiles/agents/AGENTS.md`; its done-when is two independent tests (the hook's 60-minute horizon, and the reach report's follower-registration listing), so a failure in either reads as a failure of the section.

findings.reason: stating the rehearsal's pre-state (zero claims for the rehearsal id before the announcement) is what turns "exactly one claim" into a check that can be shown to fire rather than a single observation that happens to hold.
findings.text: §4's done-when asserts "exactly one claim for the pane, and no claim from another session for the rehearsal id" but declares no negative control, unlike §1, §2 and §3 which each name one.
